experiments.name: b4_gnc_legonly_damage
experiments.baseline_commit: 46d05fe2 + cycle1 diff + this cycle's robust_leg_only code
experiments.specimen_subset: diagnostics/moonshot/synth_clean_drop{30,60}, 12 specimens each, reusing existing hierarchical placements
experiments.interpretation: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED, not a transient/environment fault: `sample_leg_nonleg_split` (fitter_3d/stratified_sampling.py, used by robust_leg_only) indexes into the TARGET mesh's face array using indices sized to the TEMPLATE's face count (20466 faces / 10235 verts). drop30/drop60 are NOT topology-preserving -- verified directly: drop30 synth_000 has 9989 verts / 19956 faces, drop60 has 9743 verts / 19456 faces, both smaller than the template. This produces an out-of-bounds CUDA index (`RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered`, `IndexKernel.cu:92 ... index out of bounds`) inside `robust_chamfer`'s `knn_points` call. Both array tasks failed identically and reproducibly (not a one-off). This is a genuine, general limitation of the leg/nonleg and distal/nondistal face-index samplers (fitter_3d/stratified_sampling.py's sample_leg_nonleg_split AND sample_target_distal_protected, i.e. also Rank 5's C5 from cycle 1) -- documented in that file's own docstring as requiring topology-preserving corpora, but this is the first time it was actually exercised on a non-topology-preserving one.
experiments.prediction_supported: N/A -- technical failure, not a scientific result
experiments.next: NOT silently patched or retried under changed parameters, per the standing execution rule. gnc_legonly and Rank 5's C5 are therefore NOT currently usable on damage/missing-geometry corpora (i.e. not usable on the real, non-topology-preserving specimen scans that are the actual production target) without new engineering: a topology-robust face-membership lookup (e.g. nearest-template-face per target point) instead of assuming identical face indexing. Flagged as a well-scoped follow-up, not attempted this cycle. Substituted a new, well-motivated, DIFFERENT arm below (gnc_medium, which uses plain global sampling with no face-index assumption and is therefore topology-agnostic) so damage-condition evidence for at least one validated GNC variant is not lost this cycle.

experiments.name: b6_gnc_legonly_topofree
experiments.command: sbatch diagnostics/cycle2_20260819/b6_gnc_legonly_topofree_damage.sbatch (array 0-1: drop30/drop60); sbatch diagnostics/cycle2_20260819/b6_gnc_legonly_topofree_n50.sbatch (array 0-1: seeds 0/1, clean N50 control)
experiments.baseline_commit: 46d05fe2 + cycle1 diff + cycle2 diff (adds robust_chamfer_leg_split_topofree + MoonshotStage.robust_leg_only_topofree in fitter_3d/trainer_moonshot.py, robust_leg_only_topofree plumbing in fitter_3d/optimise_moonshot.py, cfg/gnc_legonly_topofree.yaml)
experiments.specimen_subset: drop30 (12 specimens), drop60 (12 specimens), synth_clean_n50 (50 specimens x 2 seeds, control)
experiments.motivation: User follow-up after B4 FAILED (gnc_legonly on drop30/drop60 crashed: sample_leg_nonleg_split assumes target mesh shares template face indexing, violated by damage corpora). Implements a topology-robust variant: source-side leg/non-leg split unchanged (src_mesh is always full template topology), target-side split replaced by NN label transfer from the fitted source mesh instead of target face indices -- see robust_chamfer_leg_split_topofree docstring in fitter_3d/trainer_moonshot.py.
experiments.smoke_test: CPU smoke test (nits=3, n_sample=500) on both synth_clean_drop30 (max_meshes=2) and synth_clean_n50 (max_meshes=3) -- both completed with no crash before SLURM submission.
experiments.interpretation: topofree gnc_legonly runs cleanly on drop30/drop60 (the crash is fixed). In a SINGLE-SEED check (N=12, the existing damage corpora, no seed replication run) it matches or beats gnc_medium's R gain (drop30: +0.019 better; drop60: -0.002, tied) while costing far less on antenna quality (-2.8%/-0.5%, i.e. BETTER than baseline, vs gnc_medium's +10.2%/+12.1% cost). This damage-condition result has NOT been replicated across seeds and does not yet meet this project's own promotion bar (B1 required N>=50/2 seeds before treating the clean-data GNC result as more than provisional); a +0.019 delta at n=1 is not distinguishable from seed noise. The N50 clean-data control (2 seeds) DOES meet the promotion bar and shows only a -0.009 R difference vs B1's exact-label gnc_legonly -- but a follow-up probe (b6_probe_label_transfer.py) found this small aggregate difference masks a real mechanism-level effect: the NN-based target-label transfer disagrees with the true face-based label 12.2% of the time (72k points, 12 specimens), split evenly between true-leg->predicted-nonleg (6.2%) and true-nonleg->predicted-leg (6.0%). This is NOT a topology-match/noise artifact that vanishes with correspondence quality -- it is a structural property of NN label transfer at finite sample density, concentrated at the leg/body boundary. The aggregate R is robust to this per-point noise, but the boundary disagreement rate is high enough to be relevant to the Track A2 within-leg mismatch story if topofree-labeled data is ever used for that analysis (A2 itself did NOT use any leg_only/topofree run -- confirmed by inspection of a2_within_leg_deepdive.py's `conditions` list, which only references baseline _w5 runs -- so A2's existing B5 gate decision is unaffected by this finding).
experiments.prediction_supported: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED, with an important qualifier the user correctly flagged: the damage-condition result (beats/ties gnc_medium) is a SINGLE-SEED finding, not yet replicated, and should be read as "provisionally promising, replication pending" rather than a settled result. The clean-data control DOES meet the project's promotion bar (N=50, 2 seeds) and confirms topofree is a safe, low-cost substitute for exact-label gnc_legonly there. Status: topofree gnc_legonly is the preferred candidate for clean/topology-preserving data (promotion bar met); on damage data it is provisionally promising, not yet promoted past experimental (replication pending, same bar B1 applied to clean-data GNC before trusting it).
experiments.collateral_regressions: none observed in aggregate mesh quality (degenerate_tri_frac=0.0, folded_face_frac comparable). A real but non-regressive mechanism-level effect WAS found: 12.2% target-point mislabeling rate at the leg/body boundary (see b6_probe_label_transfer.py) -- does not show up as an aggregate R regression but is a genuine property of the method, not noise.
experiments.next: (1) N>=50/multi-seed replication on damage corpora before any stronger promotion claim -- same bar B1 applied to clean data. (2) real-specimen (non-synthetic) validation remains untested. (3) the 12.2% boundary-relabeling rate is a mechanism worth investigating further if within-leg mismatch work is revisited on topofree-labeled data specifically.

experiments.name: b6_probe_label_transfer
experiments.baseline_commit: 46d05fe2 + cycle1 diff + cycle2 diff (no new code needed, replays MoonshotStage.forward's topofree branch offline using the converged N50_gnc_legonly_topofree_seed0 fit)
experiments.specimen_subset: synth_clean_n50, first 12 specimens (subset for speed), topology-preserving corpus (required so ground-truth face labels exist on the target side for comparison)
experiments.output_path: stdout only (no artifact file; deterministic given the same converged .npz input)
experiments.interpretation: Answers the user's question directly from the code and an empirical replay, not just the aggregate metric: NN-based target-label transfer does NOT reduce to the exact face-based split even when topology matches perfectly. 12.2% of target points get a different leg/non-leg kernel treatment than their true face membership would assign, symmetrically in both directions (not a directional bias). Mechanistically this is because target points are drawn by generic uniform sampling (not restricted to a face pool) and their label comes from nearest-neighbour distance to a SPARSE, randomly-drawn set of source points (not the literal nearest source vertex) -- at finite sample density this misclassifies points near the leg/body boundary regardless of registration quality. The B6 aggregate R result is not sensitive to this (topofree still matches/beats gnc_medium and barely differs from exact gnc_legonly), but the effect is real and structurally explained, not just observed as "no regression" in aggregate.
experiments.prediction_supported: user's hypothesis (that this deserved verification from the code, not just the aggregate metric) was correct: the mechanisms are NOT identical
experiments.next: if within-leg mismatch (Track A2) is ever re-analyzed using topofree-labeled data, this 12.2% boundary effect should be accounted for explicitly

experiments.name: a1_pca_taxonomy_v2_adjudication
experiments.command: python diagnostics/cycle2_20260819/a1_pca_taxonomy_v2.py; plus one ad-hoc joint-residualization follow-up (size+chamfer_l2 together) run inline, not saved as a separate script
experiments.baseline_commit: 46d05fe2 + cycle1 diff + cycle2 diff (analysis-only, no new fitting jobs, no new dependencies)
experiments.specimen_subset: same as a1_pca_taxonomy (v1): 80 ALL_ANTS_CLEAN specimens x 3 seeds, 60 labeled/20 unlabeled split
experiments.seed: rng seed 0 for permutation tests and random-pair reference draws (20000 permutations)
experiments.start_time: 2026-08-19T (this turn, user: do not let A1 go out half-adjudicated)
experiments.interpretation: Ran all 4 checks the user specified before treating v1's headline finding as more than a lead. (1) Permutation test (20000 draws, n=4 genera sizes 2/3/2/4): the raw non-articulated baseline's genus clustering IS statistically significant despite the small n (size-inclusive p=0.025, scale-invariant-only p=0.020); fitted betas' non-clustering is a clean null (p=0.772), not underpowered noise near the boundary. (2) Size confound: caught and fixed a real v1 error -- the "non-articulated baseline" was NOT actually scale-invariant (included raw extents + volume proxy). Rebuilt as aspect-ratios-only: clusters just as well (p=0.020), so the baseline's advantage is NOT a size artifact. Separately, beta PC1 correlates strongly with centroid size (r=0.706) but residualizing against it does not rescue clustering (p=0.785, unchanged). (3) Registration-artifact covariate -- the most important finding: beta PC1 (41.7% of variance) correlates at r=0.722 with chamfer_l2 and r=-0.778 with fscore@0.01 -- the CURRENT shape space's dominant axis is overwhelmingly explained by per-specimen fit quality, not anatomy. This is real and independently important (affects trust in this shape space for any downstream use) regardless of the taxonomy question. Follow-up: residualized against BOTH centroid size AND chamfer_l2 jointly -- genus clustering STILL does not appear (p=0.863, moved further from significance). So the registration-quality confound is real but is not, by itself, why genus clustering is absent. (4) Confirmed (not just claimed) that the 20/80 unlabeled specimens are excluded from every statistic, and fixed a real data-leakage channel in v1 (z-scoring used all 80 specimens' mean/std including unlabeled ones; v2 standardizes on labeled-only statistics).
experiments.prediction_supported: The user's concern was well-founded on all 4 points, and each check surfaced something real: (1) confirmed the baseline result is significant despite small n, not noise; (2) caught and fixed an actual bug in v1's baseline description (it was not scale-invariant as claimed); (3) found a real, important, independent registration-quality confound in the shape space (r=0.72), though it does not explain away the null clustering result; (4) confirmed exclusion and fixed a real normalization-leakage bug. Net: the headline finding survives adjudication and can now go to Fabian as a checked result, with the registration-quality entanglement flagged as an equally important, independent finding.
experiments.next: investigate the registration-quality entanglement in beta PC1 on its own terms (separate from the taxonomy question); test nonlinear confound removal (only linear OLS residualization was checked here); expand the multi-specimen-genus test set if more replicated ALL_ANTS_CLEAN-style specimens exist; resolve the 20/80 unlabeled-specimen taxonomy gap.

experiments.name: a1_pca_taxonomy_v3_followups
experiments.baseline_commit: 46d05fe2 + cycle1 diff + cycle2 diff (analysis-only, no new fitting jobs, no new dependencies, reuses v2 helpers via import)
experiments.specimen_subset: same 80 ALL_ANTS_CLEAN specimens x 3 seeds; classification tests restricted to the 11 specimens across the 4 multi-member genera (singleton-genus specimens cannot be evaluated in a leave-one-out task)
experiments.seed: rng seed 0; 5000 permutations per classification test (reduced from 20000 for runtime -- pure-python LOO loop)
experiments.start_time: 2026-08-19T (this turn, user: three specific follow-ups before v2 counts as settled)

primary_metrics.high_fit_quality_subsample_status: degenerate -- 0/4 genera retain >=2 specimens after top-half fscore filter

experiments.interpretation: Follow-up 1 (LOO classification, the actual field-standard test the user specified): raw betas 1-NN accuracy 0.455 (p=0.087, borderline, NOT below conventional significance) -- genuinely different from v2's flat unsupervised ratio-test null (p=0.77), exactly the failure mode the user's point predicted (a signal on non-top-2 PCs invisible to an unsupervised ratio). Does not replicate under nearest-centroid classification on the same features (p=0.213) or after removing the known size/fit-quality confound (residualized 1-NN accuracy drops to 0.273, p=0.400, WORSE not better) -- most parsimoniously explained by the same confound v2 already found, not an independent rescued signal, though this is genuinely borderline. Follow-up 2 (deform_verts, Fabian's original explicit request, not tested until now): reduced to top-10 PCA components (40% variance explained, notably flatter than betas' concentration). Cross-seed repeatability 345.6 (real signal, noisier than betas' 613 as expected for a less-regularized descriptor). Deform PC1 shows an EVEN STRONGER registration-quality entanglement than betas (r=-0.804 vs betas' 0.722) -- consistent with deformation magnitude being close to a direct proxy for how much correction fitting needed. No genus clustering (ratio 1.248, p=0.779) and no classification signal (1-NN accuracy 0.182, actually BELOW the null mean of 0.198). Testing deformations does not rescue the taxonomy signal; if anything the free-form residual is more confounded by fit quality than the regularized beta prior. Follow-up 3 (high-fit-quality subsample, nonlinear-robustness check): DEGENERATE at this sample size -- restricting to top-half fscore specimens eliminates all within-genus pairs across all 4 multi-member genera (0/4 retain >=2 specimens). Reported honestly as a real limitation, not forced onto a degenerate subset.
experiments.prediction_supported: The user's three concerns were each addressed and each surfaced something real: (1) the supervised classification test DID find something the unsupervised ratio test missed (borderline 1-NN signal, p=0.087) -- validates the concern that PCA-null does not equal no-signal, even though this specific signal did not survive further scrutiny; (2) deform_verts does not change the conclusion and if anything shows a WORSE registration-quality confound than betas -- a genuine, new, useful negative result answering Fabian's original explicit request; (3) the nonlinear-robustness check could not be run at this sample size -- an honest methodological finding, not a null result either way. Net: the core adjudicated finding (no clean, reliable genus-clustering signal in the current fitted shape space) survives all three follow-ups, with the single limiting factor across every single check being sample size (n=11 classification examples across 4 genera), not analysis choices.
experiments.next: the highest-value next step for A1 is more multi-specimen-genus data if it exists -- every check in v2 and v3 was limited by the same n=11-across-4-genera ceiling. Secondary: investigate the registration-quality confound (now confirmed in both beta AND deformation space) on its own terms, independent of the taxonomy question. Resolve the 20/80 unlabeled-specimen taxonomy gap. Install umap-learn if wanted.
